source: Shared replacement and conversion catalogue for compatible simulated engines, including factory-turbo engines. Stock hardware remains available separately. Generic family sizes are nominal installation sizes; boost tuning does not change hardware. Generic fixed-size variants are labelled by compressor inducer diameter; exducer diameter follows the anchor 66/82 wheel ratio. Their similarity-scaled flow, inertia, mass and dimensions are fixed by the selected diameter, not by engine demand or boost. Generic estimates, not manufacturer performance maps.
anchor_exducer_source: Reference compressor exducer for similarity scaling and card dimensions. Anchor wheel ratio: 66 mm inducer / 82 mm exducer (anchor rotor_inertia_source).

sizing.volumetric_efficiency_source: [AS] a street engine near its power peak; the demand is an upper estimate at the limiter.
sizing.flow_margin_source: [AS] compressor max flow 40 % above the engine's peak need: room before choke at the limiter without the lag of a much larger wheel.
sizing.efficiency_log_slope_source: [AS] efficiency = anchor 0.80 + 0.127 ln(s): a wheel half the anchor's size reaches ~0.71 (small passenger-car turbos peak at 0.70-0.75), clamped to [efficiency_min, anchor].
sizing.wastegate_to_throat_source: physics_sim turbo templates: wastegate port 3.0 x the turbine throat (a single on a small engine; the anchor's twin uses 2.36).

conversion.max_compression_ratio_source: physics_sim engine.md: a converted engine keeps the compression ratio at or below 10.5 (check_buildable's forced-induction ceiling); 10.0 leaves knock margin on E5 [AS]. Engines below it keep theirs.

boost_control.source: physics_sim turbo configuration templates (gains per unit of target_boost_bar).

kits_help: Choose single, twin or quad induction in Swaps, then select a fixed compressor inducer size in mm under Engine > Turbo. Boost is adjusted separately in Tuning and never resizes installed hardware. Bay fit is checked; existing auto-sized saved kits remain supported.

envelope.source: [AS] one turbo unit as a box from its compressor exducer D: length along the shaft 2.6 D + 60 mm (compressor housing, bearing housing, turbine housing), outer size 2.2 D (the compressor volute). Anchor GTX3582R class, D 82 mm: 273 x 180 mm, about its catalogue outline. Units sit in a row along the crank on the exhaust side (a V engine with more than one: split over both banks), 20 mm apart; the row sets the length when it is longer than the engine. Width: the turbo takes the place of the NA exhaust manifold, which the engine envelope already holds, so only half its outer size (unit_side_protrusion 0.5) stands out on that side. The charge pipe (sized for 60 m/s at charge density per unit, for its mass) is routed through the gaps to the front-mounted intercooler ahead of the radiator; neither is in the box (open question: no bay model of the gaps).

mass.source: [AS] Turbo unit: 2.0 kg that do not shrink with the wheel (bearing housing, oil/water lines, actuator) + 7.5 kg x s^3 (housings scale with volume): the anchor (s = 1) 9.5 kg, a GTX3582R-class unit with housings; s = 0.44 (a small single on a 1 L three) 2.6 kg, a K03-class unit. Exhaust manifold and downpipe 3 kg per turbo. Intercooler: a 600 x 300 x 76 mm bar-and-plate core (~9 kg) serves about 0.4 kg/s, so 0.45 m2 of face per kg/s, 76 mm deep, 650 kg/m3 effective (core + end tanks). Charge piping: 1.8 m compressor -> intercooler -> throttle, +0.6 m per extra turbo; its mass per metre comes from the material below.

limits.source: Damage-model data, not simulated yet. [AS] a rotor's rated maximum shaft speed is 15 % above the scaled reference speed (compressor maps end near the tip-speed limit; the reference speed is the map's design point). The advisor warns when the dyno sweep's rotor speed passes it.

piping.label: Plastic
piping.source: [AS] moulded PA66 charge pipes with rubber couplers as on factory turbo cars: rated for the factory boost (about 1 to 1.5 bar); couplers blow off and pipes crack near 3 bar. PA66-GF density 1350 kg/m3, 3 mm wall.

piping.label: Aluminium
piping.source: [AS] mandrel-bent 6061 tube with silicone couplers and T-bolt clamps: the couplers limit it to about 3 bar continuous; the tube itself holds far more. 2 mm wall, 2700 kg/m3.

piping.label: Stainless steel
piping.source: [AS] 304 stainless tube with welded beads and reinforced 4-ply silicone couplers / V-band joints: about 5 bar continuous. 1.5 mm wall, 7900 kg/m3.
